title: RecordContribution — portable skill interchange structure
description: Schema for a RecordContribution, per shared/record-contribution.md. A contribution is an interpretation: this evidence may contribute this semantic value to this organisational object. It references at least one SourceFragment, and its interpreted value must be supported by those spans. Contribution is many-to-many: one fragment may contribute to several objects, and one object draws from many fragments. This is NOT a record schema — it carries no organisational authority and cannot admit anything to organisational truth. See TDR-0018.

fragment_refs.description: One or more `fragment_id` values. At least one: a contribution with no fragment behind it is an invention.

target_object.description: The organisational object being reconstructed — `consequential-decision`, `ovc`, or an object supplied by a later record package. Deliberately an open pattern rather than an enum: the contract must extend to objects whose record status is still unsettled.

target_record_type.description: The record type that would preserve that object — `TDR`, `VR`. Carried alongside `target_object` because the object is what is reconstructed, while the record is how it would be preserved.

semantic_role.description: The role within the target object. Defined by the record package, not by this schema. A role invented at interpretation time cannot be validated later.

interpreted_value.description: What the skill reads the evidence as saying for that role. Absence is never expressed here — a missing semantic is reported by the CandidateAssembly, not as an empty contribution.

extraction_confidence.description: Did I read these words correctly?

epistemic_confidence.description: How strong is the underlying evidence for the claim? Independent of extraction_confidence — a source may state a number plainly while the number is unsupported.

derivation.description: Optional: how the interpreted value was derived — read directly from the referenced span(s) (explicit), or inferred across spans or from context (inferred). Record-neutral and additive (TDR-0026): instances without it remain valid. Derivation is reported alongside a candidate's completeness view and is never folded into its state grades — an inferred proposition must not present as complete, and an incomplete one must not hide behind 'inferred'.

confidence.description: The standard's existing ladder (spec.md §4.1). A judgement, not a calibrated probability: no arithmetic, no averaging, no composite score.
